limitations_and_boundaries: GCNII requires tuning of hyperparameters αℓ and βℓ.
Theoretical analysis assumes connected self-looped graph.
Experiments limited to citation networks, web networks, and PPI; generalization to other graph types not tested.
GCNII* uses more parameters due to separate weight matrices.
Over-smoothing analysis focuses on GCN with residual connection, not all GNN variants.
Future work needed to combine with attention and analyze ReLU behavior.

research_questions.statement: How can we design a deep graph convolutional network that prevents over-smoothing and achieves state-of-the-art performance?

provenance.text_excerpt: Our results successfully demonstrate that GCNII and GCNII* achieves new state-of-the-art performance across all three datasets.

claims.statement: GCNII achieves new state-of-the-art performance on semi-supervised node classification on Cora, Citeseer, and Pubmed.

provenance.text_excerpt: Overall, the results suggest that with initial residual and identity mapping, we can resolve the over-smoothing problem and extend the vanilla GCN into a truly deep model.

claims.statement: Initial residual and identity mapping together resolve over-smoothing and enable deep GCN.

provenance.text_excerpt: 1) Directly applying identity mapping to the vanilla GCN retards the effect of over-smoothing marginally. 2) Directly applying initial residual connection to the vanilla GCN relieves over-smoothing significantly. However, the best performance is still achieved by the 2-layer model. 3) Applying identity mapping and initial residual connection simultaneously ensures that the accuracy increases with the network depths.

results.value_raw_text: Ablation: identity mapping alone marginally retards over-smoothing; initial residual alone relieves but best at 2 layers; both together ensure accuracy increases with depth.

provenance.text_excerpt: To extend GCN to a truly deep model, we need to enable GCN to express a K order polynomial filter with arbitrary coefficients. We show this can be achieved by two simple techniques: Initial residual connection and Identity mapping.

claims.statement: GCNII can express a K-order polynomial filter with arbitrary coefficients, overcoming the fixed-coefficient limitation of vanilla GCN.

provenance.text_excerpt: Our analysis suggests that the converge rate of an individual node depends on its degree, and we conduct experiments to back up this theoretical finding.

claims.statement: In multi-layer GCN with residual connection, nodes with higher degrees are more likely to suffer from over-smoothing.

Theoretical analysis showing GCNII can express a K-order polynomial filter with arbitrary coefficients.

methods.name: GCNII
methods.protocol_description: GCNII extends vanilla GCN with two techniques: initial residual connection (skip connection from input layer H(0)) and identity mapping (adding identity matrix In to weight matrix W(ℓ)). Layer update: H(ℓ+1) = σ(((1-αℓ)˜P H(ℓ) + αℓ H(0)) ((1-βℓ)In + βℓ W(ℓ))). αℓ is typically 0.1 or 0.2; βℓ = log(λ/(ℓ+1)) ≈ λ/ℓ.

methods.name: GCNII*
methods.protocol_description: Variant of GCNII that uses different weight matrices for smoothed representation and initial residual: H(ℓ+1) = σ((1-αℓ)˜P H(ℓ) ((1-βℓ)In + βℓ W1(ℓ)) + αℓ H(0) ((1-βℓ)In + βℓ W2(ℓ))).

study_units.name: GCNII model proposal and theoretical analysis
